sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
A sentiment dashboard answers what. Intelligence has to answer why. SAGA is not a social media monitoring tool, a sentiment dashboard, a listening platform or a keyword tracker — it combines those into one intelligence ecosystem, which only works if the engine beneath them is shared.

Conversations move faster than reports

A claim, a grievance or a controversy crosses platforms in hours. A weekly report arrives after the damage is done.

The signals sit in different places

Social platforms, news portals, forums, review sites and client data each arrive in their own format, language and access method.

Every finding has to stand up

Sources, timestamps, hashes and analyst actions must be preserved, because an AI assessment is not evidence on its own.

01 See02 Understand03 Connect04 Measure 05 Verify06 Detect07 Decide & act
Four workspaces

Four verticals, four different screens.

A common dashboard across all four would make the product look generic and weaken its positioning. The shell is shared — navigation rail, context bar, canvas — but each vertical lays out its own panels, in its own order, with its own component types, terminology, scoring model and permissions.

Collection depth

Three tiers of the web, one collection layer.

Most monitoring tools read only what a search engine already indexes. SAGA collects across three distinct tiers, each with its own retrieval method, its own authorisation requirement and its own controls. All three converge on the same normalisation layer, so a finding carries the same provenance regardless of where it came from.

T1 · Surface web
Indexed and openly reachable

Everything a standard search engine can already reach: public pages, public profiles and openly published content. This is the volume tier — it sets the baseline the other two are measured against.

Retrieved by
Social platforms through official APIs or licensed data providers only; news and open websites by scheduled collection of permitted pages; syndication feeds and licensed aggregators.
Authorisation
Platform terms only. No scraping where a platform restricts it.
Used for
Narrative detection, sentiment baseline, trend and momentum, media and review intelligence.
T2 · Deep web
Reachable, but not indexed

Content that exists publicly or under licence but sits behind a search form, a login the client holds, a paywall or a database query, so no crawler returns it. This is the corroboration tier: where a claim seen on the surface is checked against a record.

Retrieved by
Query-driven lookups — never blanket crawling — licensed feeds, and credentials the client owns and authorises.
Authorisation
Written authorisation recorded per source; queries tied to a case or mandate.
Used for
Entity corroboration, record verification, evidence support, historical archives.
T3 · Dark web
Overlay networks, authorised engagements only

Sites reachable only through overlay networks. This is the early-warning tier: it exists to tell a client that something of theirs has surfaced where it should not have. Collection is read-only and the platform never participates in what it observes.

Retrieved by
An isolated, hardened collection environment; read-only monitoring of openly visible listings, matched against the client's declared assets.
Authorisation
Legal sign-off and a defined mandate before the tier is switched on. Enabled per engagement, not by default.
Used for
Leak and exposure indicators, credential-exposure signals for client-owned assets only under the client's mandate, threat early warning, brand misuse detection.
What the platform never does, at any tier
No access to private accounts, inboxes or closed groups No credential cracking, bypassing or sharing No purchases, bids or transactions No undercover personas or contact with operators No retention or display of illegal material: it is filtered at collection and incidents go to legal No tier enabled without the client's written mandate

Depth is scoped, not assumed. Surface collection runs by default. Deep and dark tiers are enabled per engagement, with their coverage stated source by source in the deployment document — because what is reachable differs by country, by platform and by the authorisation the client holds.

Fast for the analyst. Defensible for the organisation.

  • Lawful collection only — publicly accessible and authorised sources, within platform terms and applicable law.
  • Every action logged — searches, scans, results and sign-offs recorded with the analyst who performed them.
  • Similarity is not attribution — the platform can show that two accounts look related; it cannot establish who owns one.
  • A human decides — AI output is decision support. Negative sentiment is never treated as evidence of an offence.
  • Not a poll — online discussion is not representative sampling and is never presented as voting intention.
  • No profiling of private citizens — public conversation is read in aggregate; no profile of a private individual or record of a citizen's political views is built.
  • Not a targeting tool — never used to target, persuade or act against individuals for political ends, including micro-targeting of voters.
  • One method for every party — models, scoring and thresholds are applied identically and checked for skew.
  • Provenance preserved — source, timestamp and hash travel with the finding, because an AI assessment is not admissible alone.
Established
  • Positioning as a digital intelligence platform

  • Goodwill and trust scoring as core positioning
  • Language understanding beyond keywords
  • Narrative and trend detection
  • Executive-grade intelligence dashboards

This separation matters in every proposal: a proposed capability is never presented as an operational one.

sections.title: Data protection & compliance
sections.html:
Data protection & compliance

Personal data handled to Indian law, in the client's jurisdiction.

SAGA is designed to support the client's obligations under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025, which come into force in phases through May 2027.

Purpose limitation

Every workspace, watchlist and query is tied to a recorded purpose and mandate. Data collected for one purpose is not reused for another without a new authorisation.

Data minimisation

Only the fields a stated purpose needs are kept. Identifiers that analysis does not need are masked or dropped at ingestion.

Consent and lawful basis

Client-provided personal data, such as CRM or complaint records, is processed only on the basis the client records: consent, or another use the Act permits.

Data residency

Stored and processed in India by default: in the client's chosen cloud region or in their own data centre. No transfer outside India without written approval.

Retention and erasure

Retention is set per source and workspace by contract, with deletion at expiry. Correction and erasure requests run through the client's grievance process.

Breach response

Security incidents are logged and reported to the client, with the records the client needs to notify the Data Protection Board and affected individuals.

Each deployment's position under the Act is confirmed with the client's legal team before go-live.

sections.title: Deployment models
sections.html:
Deployment models

Cloud, private cloud, on-premise or air-gapped.

The same platform runs in four ways. The choice follows the client's data classification.

Managed cloud

Run by Blue Cloud in an India cloud region. Fastest to start; suited to brand, celebrity and pilot engagements.

Private cloud

Dedicated tenancy in the client's own cloud account or an approved government cloud, on an isolated network, with keys the client holds.

On-premise

Installed in the client's data centre. All collected data, models and logs stay on client infrastructure; support works under the client's access controls.

Air-gapped

The analysis environment has no internet connection. Collection runs in a separate environment and data enters through a controlled, logged transfer. For classified police and government use.

Tenant isolation and data segregation

Separate data per client

Each client's data sits in its own logically separate store with its own encryption keys. On private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployments the separation is physical.

Separate workspaces

Inside one client, verticals, departments and cases are separate workspaces with their own users, watchlists and retention.

No cross-client learning

One client's data, labels and analyst corrections are not used to train models that serve another client.

sections.title: AI governance
sections.html:
AI governance

Models are versioned, measured and corrected by analysts.

AI output is decision support, so the models behind it get the same scrutiny as the findings.

Model versioning

Every finding records the model and version that produced it. Model changes go out through a change log, with rollback.

Analyst feedback loop

Analysts correct sentiment, entity and classification labels on screen. Corrections are reviewed, then used to recalibrate and retrain.

Accuracy monitoring

Accuracy is measured per language and per vertical against labelled samples, and reported to the client. A language goes live only after it meets the agreed threshold.

Bias review

Scoring is reviewed for skew across parties, regions, languages and communities before each release, and on a fixed schedule after it.

Explainable scores

Every score shows the posts and factors behind it, so an analyst can say why a number moved.

Human sign-off

No automated action is taken against a person. Escalations, reports and evidence packages are signed by a named officer.
